source: Lingfern original course explanations; definitions remain draft; selected sense mappings reviewed by Codex/AI

entries.definition: A set of pages with words or pictures that you can read.
entries.example: Bring a book to the reading group.

entries.definition: An object you use to write with ink.
entries.example: Write your name with a pen.

entries.definition: Something you carry things in.
entries.example: Put your book in your bag.

entries.definition: A small container you drink from.
entries.example: This is a cup of water.

entries.definition: A place where you can read or borrow books.
entries.example: Meet me at the library.

entries.definition: Take something with you to a place.
entries.example: Bring your student card.

entries.definition: A card that shows you are a student.
entries.example: Show your student card at the desk.

entries.definition: A book of empty pages for writing notes.
entries.example: You do not need a notebook today.

entries.definition: An object you write or draw with; it usually has a graphite point.
entries.example: Bring a pencil to the art club.

entries.definition: A thin material you can write or draw on.
entries.example: Paper is on the table.

entries.definition: A piece of furniture with a flat top.
entries.example: The paper is on the table.

entries.definition: A place where people buy drinks and small meals.
entries.example: The art club meets at the café.

entries.definition: A place where people can see objects about art, history or science.
entries.example: The museum opens at eleven on Friday.

entries.definition: A paper or digital record that lets you enter a place or use a service.
entries.example: Get your ticket at the front desk.

entries.definition: Get to a place.
entries.example: Please arrive after the doors open.

entries.definition: Start allowing people to enter or use a place.
entries.example: The studio opens at noon.

entries.definition: Stop allowing people to enter or use a place.
entries.example: The museum closes at five.

entries.definition: The place near an entrance where staff help visitors.
entries.example: Ask at the front desk for Room Twelve.

entries.definition: A space inside a building, with walls around it.
entries.example: The group meets in Room Twelve.

entries.definition: A time when people come together to talk or plan.
entries.example: The staff have a meeting this morning.

entries.definition: A room or building where people can see works of art.
entries.example: The staff prepare the gallery on Thursday.

entries.definition: A group of people learning together.
entries.example: The beginners’ class starts at half past ten.

entries.definition: A place filled with water where people can swim.
entries.example: The pool opens at ten this Saturday.

entries.definition: Only if a stated condition is met. In a recommendation, it introduces a condition on support.
entries.example: We support the trial provided a staffed walk-in period remains.

entries.definition: Acknowledging a point that supports another view, without necessarily accepting that whole view.
entries.example: The writer concedes that appointments reduce waiting, but objects to booking-only access.

entries.definition: Responsible for a decision or action and expected to explain or correct it.
entries.example: A named catalogue team remains accountable for the published description.

entries.definition: Allowing only one route or group and excluding alternatives.
entries.example: The objection concerns an exclusive online route into the service.

entries.definition: A formal message asking someone to give you something or do something for you.
entries.example: Send a request for the library book.

entries.definition: Prepared and available for you to use or collect.
entries.example: Wait for a message saying that your book is ready.

entries.definition: A room where people prepare and cook food.
entries.example: We cook in the kitchen.

entries.definition: A room where people sleep.
entries.example: I sleep in the bedroom.

entries.definition: A room with a bath or shower, where people wash.
entries.example: I wash in the bathroom.

entries.definition: A room where people sit and relax at home.
entries.example: We relax in the living room.

entries.definition: Rest and feel calm.
entries.example: I relax in the living room.

entries.definition: Prepare food so people can eat it.
entries.example: We cook in the kitchen.

entries.definition: A room or building where people exercise.
entries.example: Where is the gym?

entries.definition: A room where people collect or sort letters and other mail.
entries.example: This is the mailroom.

entries.definition: A room where people can sit and relax.
entries.example: The gym is across from the lounge.

entries.definition: Exercise to keep your body strong and healthy.
entries.example: I want to work out.

entries.definition: Very close to the side of someone or something.
entries.example: The gym is next to the mailroom.

entries.definition: On the other side, facing someone or something.
entries.example: The gym is across from the lounge.

entries.definition: Very good or exciting. This is informal language.
entries.example: Things are awesome!

entries.definition: On or towards a higher floor in a building.
entries.example: Let’s go upstairs!

entries.definition: Doing something that needs your time and attention.
entries.example: Right now I am busy.

entries.definition: Save sound or video so that people can play it later.
entries.example: I have to record again.

entries.definition: A programme made for an audience.
entries.example: I am doing my show!

entries.definition: One more time.
entries.example: Can I read again?

entries.definition: A person who works with you.
entries.example: Please meet your co-workers.

entries.definition: A room where people make or record programmes.
entries.example: May I see the studio?

entries.definition: The part of the day between midday and evening.
entries.example: Come by this afternoon.

entries.definition: Say that you are sorry for something you did.
entries.example: Today I want to apologize to my co-workers.

entries.definition: A distinct speech sound that can distinguish words in a language.
entries.example: The word “cat” has three phonemes.

entries.definition: Related to the sounds people make when they speak.
entries.example: The phonetic alphabet uses symbols for sounds.

entries.definition: A written sign that represents a sound, idea or thing.
entries.example: A special symbol can show a phoneme.

entries.definition: Lasting for a very short time.
entries.example: A state of being is longer than a momentary feeling.

entries.definition: A condition describing how a person feels or experiences life over a period of time.
entries.example: In retirement, her state of being became more relaxed.

entries.definition: Connect one thing with another.
entries.example: The verb can link a subject with its description.

entries.definition: A word used to name a person, place, thing or idea.
entries.example: Farmer is a noun.

entries.definition: A word used to describe a noun.
entries.example: Rich is an adjective.

entries.definition: A set of rooms where someone lives.
entries.example: Anna lives in an apartment.

entries.definition: A person you share a room or apartment with.
entries.example: Anna and Marsha are roommates.

entries.definition: A large shop where people buy food and things for their home.
entries.example: Is there a supermarket near here?

entries.definition: The main meal of the day, often eaten in the evening.
entries.example: I want to cook dinner.

entries.definition: A telephone number for a different person from the one you want to call.
entries.example: You have the wrong number.

entries.definition: With a name after it, asks someone to use that name for you. It can also ask someone to phone you.
entries.example: Please call me Caty. (Use this name.) / Please call me later. (Phone me.)
